name: Visa-Free Entry (365 days)

qualifying_event.description: Citizens of countries listed in the Government of Georgia's ordinance (which includes most EU/EEA states, the UK, the US, Canada, Australia, Japan, and many others) may enter and remain in Georgia without a visa for one full year (365 days), holding a valid passport (or, for EU citizens, an EU-issued identity card, or a UN Laissez-Passer for eligible holders).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Valid passport or qualifying travel document from a listed country.

value.note: Nationals of the countries listed in the Government of Georgia ordinance annex.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires citizenship of a country listed in the ordinance's annex.

evidence_required.document: Valid passport, EU identity card, or UN Laissez-Passer (as applicable)

outcome.duration_length: up to 365 days (1 full year) per stay

sources.title: Legislative Herald of Georgia (matsne.gov.ge) -- Government of Georgia Ordinance on the List of Countries Whose Citizens May Enter Georgia Without a Visa

notes: NEW COUNTRY, first Georgia route. This is an unusually generous visa-free allowance by international standards -- 365 days, not the more typical 90/180-day Schengen-style rule -- confirmed directly from the government's own ordinance text. A SEPARATE ordinance (matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/2867377) grants a narrower 90-days-per-180-days allowance specifically to holders of a valid visa or residence permit from a second list of ~50 countries (even if they are not citizens of those countries) -- a distinct, additional route not modelled separately here since it is a narrower variant of the same 'visit' category rather than a materially different legal status. No financial-means or purpose-of-visit conditions are stated in the ordinance itself. This visa-free period is commonly used in practice by remote workers/'digital nomads' -- Georgia does not currently operate a dedicated digital-nomad-visa legal category (its pandemic-era 'Remotely from Georgia' program has lapsed into ordinary business/work-permit channels), so no separate digital_nomad route is modelled for this country; see ge_it_professional_permit and ge_investment_residence_permit for the actual legal pathways remote workers use to stay longer term.
